exposure: educated labor attendant (ELA) presence during labor
cohort: The study included 252 pregnant women, divided into two groups (126 in each) based on the presence or absence of an educated labor attendant during labor.
finding: The presence of an educated labor attendant (ELA) significantly reduced the rate of cesarean section, need for systemic analgesics, and pain measurements, while increasing postpartum parenting behavior and labor agentry scores.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean section was significantly lower in the group with an educated labor attendant.
